606:             barycenter_size=barycenter_size,
607:             init_barycenter=init_barycenter,
608:             max_iter=max_iter,
609:             tol=tol,
610:             weights=weights,
611:             metric_params=metric_params,
612:             verbose=verbose,
613:             n_jobs=n_jobs
614:         )
615:         if loss < best_cost:
616:             best_cost = loss
617:             best_barycenter = bary
618:     return best_barycenter
619: 
620: 
621: def dtw_barycenter_averaging_one_init(
622:     X,
623:     barycenter_size=None,
624:     init_barycenter=None,
625:     max_iter=30,
626:     tol=1e-5,
627:     weights=None,
628:     metric_params=None,
629:     verbose=False,
630:     n_jobs=None
631: ):
632:     """DTW Barycenter Averaging (DBA) method estimated through
633:     Expectation-Maximization algorithm.
634: 
635:     DBA was originally presented in [1]_.
636:     This implementation is based on a idea from [2]_ (Majorize-Minimize Mean
637:     Algorithm).
638: 
639:     Parameters
640:     ----------
641:     X : array-like, shape=(n_ts, sz, d)
642:         Time series dataset.
643: 
644:     barycenter_size : int or None (default: None)
645:         Size of the barycenter to generate. If None, the size of the barycenter
646:         is that of the data provided at fit
647:         time or that of the initial barycenter if specified.
648: 
649:     init_barycenter : array or None (default: None)
650:         Initial barycenter to start from for the optimization process.
651: 
652:     max_iter : int (default: 30)
653:         Number of iterations of the Expectation-Maximization optimization
654:         procedure.
655: 
656:     tol : float (default: 1e-5)
657:         Tolerance to use for early stopping: if the decrease in cost is lower
658:         than this value, the
659:         Expectation-Maximization procedure stops.
660: 
661:     weights: None or array
662:         Weights of each X[i]. Must be the same size as len(X).
663:         If None, uniform weights are used.
664: 
665:     metric_params: dict or None (default: None)
666:         DTW constraint parameters to be used.
667:         See :ref:`tslearn.metrics.dtw_path <fun-tslearn.metrics.dtw_path>` for
668:         a list of accepted parameters
669:         If None, no constraint is used for DTW computations.
670: 
671:     verbose : boolean (default: False)
672:         Whether to print information about the cost at each iteration or not.
673: 
674:     n_jobs : int or None, optional (default=None)
675:         The number of jobs to run in parallel.
676:         ``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
677:         ``-1`` means using all processors. See scikit-learns'
678:         `Glossary <https://scikit-learn.org/stable/glossary.html#term-n_jobs>`__
679:         for more details.
680: 
681: 
682:     Returns
683:     -------
684:     numpy.array of shape (barycenter_size, d) or (sz, d) if barycenter_size \
685:             is None
686:         DBA barycenter of the provided time series dataset.
687:     float
688:         Associated inertia
689: 
690:     References
691:     ----------
692:     .. [1] F. Petitjean, A. Ketterlin & P. Gancarski. A global averaging method
693:        for dynamic time warping, with applications to clustering. Pattern
694:        Recognition, Elsevier, 2011, Vol. 44, Num. 3, pp. 678-693
695: 
696:     .. [2] D. Schultz and B. Jain. Nonsmooth Analysis and Subgradient Methods
697:        for Averaging in Dynamic Time Warping Spaces.
698:        Pattern Recognition, 74, 340-358.
699:     """
700:     backend = instantiate_backend("numpy")
701: 
702:     X_ = to_time_series_dataset(X, be=backend)
703:     if barycenter_size is None:
704:         barycenter_size = X_.shape[1]
705:     weights = _set_weights(weights, X_.shape[0])
706:     if init_barycenter is None:
707:         barycenter = _init_avg(X_, barycenter_size)
708:     else:
709:         barycenter_size = init_barycenter.shape[0]
710:         barycenter = to_time_series(
711:             init_barycenter,
712:             remove_nans=True,
713:             be=backend
714:         )
715:     cost_prev, cost = numpy.inf, numpy.inf
716:     for it in range(max_iter):
717:         list_p_k, cost = _mm_assignment(
718:             X_,
719:             barycenter,
720:             weights,
721:             metric_params,
722:             n_jobs
723:         )
724:         diag_sum_v_k, list_w_k = _mm_valence_warping(list_p_k, barycenter_size,
725:                                                      weights)
726:         if verbose:
727:             print("[DBA] epoch %d, cost: %.3f" % (it + 1, cost))
728:         barycenter = _mm_update_barycenter(X_, diag_sum_v_k, list_w_k)
729:         if abs(cost_prev - cost) < tol:
730:             break
731:         elif cost_prev < cost:
732:             warnings.warn("DBA loss is increasing while it should not be. "
733:                           "Stopping optimization.", ConvergenceWarning)
734:             break
735:         else:
736:             cost_prev = cost
737:     return barycenter, cost
738: 
739: 
740: def dtw_barycenter_averaging_subgradient(
741:     X,
742:     barycenter_size=None,
743:     init_barycenter=None,
744:     max_iter=30,
745:     initial_step_size=.05,
746:     final_step_size=.005,
747:     tol=1e-5,
748:     random_state=None,
749:     weights=None,
750:     metric_params=None,
751:     verbose=False
752: ):
753:     """DTW Barycenter Averaging (DBA) method estimated through subgradient
754:     descent algorithm.
755: 
756:     DBA was originally presented in [1]_.
757:     This implementation is based on a idea from [2]_ (Stochastic Subgradient
758:     Mean Algorithm).
759: 
760:     Parameters
761:     ----------
